page: Microsoft Azure F1ads_v7 is a single-core virtual machine from the Fadsv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Operating at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz, this instance features 1 physical core and 1 thread, backed by 4.0 GB of system memory. It includes 118 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Due to its dedicated high-frequency AMD core, the F1ads_v7 achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3. However, because it is limited to a single vCPU, its multi-core performance, PassMark CPU score, and database operations fall into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block cached read bandwidth is relatively weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F1ads_v7 offers an economical entry point for workloads requiring dedicated, high-frequency single-core execution without the overhead of multi-threaded resource scaling. The inclusion of 118 GB of local storage provides a resource-dense configuration for lightweight applications. It is best suited for single-threaded background tasks, lightweight automation scripts, basic web serving, and development or testing environments that benefit from high clock speeds but do not require parallel processing.
